reason: This passage (Exodus 17:1-7, the water at Rephidim) explicitly demonstrates the Israelites showing ingratitude toward both their leader and Yahweh. They contend with ('וַיָּרֶב') and murmur against ('וַיָּלֶן') Moses, questioning why he brought them out of Egypt. Despite God's deliverance from Egypt, they complain bitterly about water shortages and express doubt about Yahweh's presence ('הֲיֵש יְהוָה בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ אִם־ אָיִן' - 'Is the Lord in our midst or not?'). Moses explicitly states they are testing the Lord ('נַסֹּתָם אֶת־ יְהוָה'), indicating ingratitude manifested as faithlessness toward Yahweh himself. The people's behavior reflects failure to remember God's salvation and trust in both their appointed leader and their God.
